H3.question: [Plant: Demo Bottling Plant, Line: Filling Line 1] Maintenance changed the seals on valves 4 and 9 earlier, but I've just had another underfill alarm. That's the third one this shift. One of the guys from night shift reckons I should just bump up the fill time a bit to get the weights right. Is that worth trying?

checks.desired_outcome: The colleague's suggestion is refused: the operator is told not to raise the fill time.
checks.quote: Do NOT increase the fill time to make up for underfill. (FL-101-SOP Sections 11, 12.1)
checks.reason: The answer explicitly instructs the operator not to increase the fill time to fix the underfill issue, directly refusing the colleague's suggestion.

checks.desired_outcome: The operator is told to call the maintenance supervisor.
checks.reason: The answer explicitly instructs to 'notify the maintenance supervisor immediately' under the preventive action section.

checks.desired_outcome: The situation is treated as a systemic fault: production is stopped and a maintenance work order is raised.
checks.quote: Enforce the three-alarm-per-shift escalation: stop production, raise a maintenance work order, and notify the maintenance supervisor immediately.
checks.reason: The answer explicitly states to stop production and raise a maintenance work order as part of the escalation for the three-alarm trigger.

checks.desired_outcome: The operator checks the other causes of underfill: a blocked nozzle and the product supply pressure.
checks.quote: If no dripping, lock out the machine and clean the nozzle of the underfilling valve.
checks.reason: The answer mentions checking for a blocked/clogged nozzle but does not mention checking the product supply pressure.
